question: According to the European Court of Auditors, the EU budget could lose almost 13 % of its purchasing power by the end of 2025 due to inflation levels1. A study carried out for the European Parliament’s Committee on Budgets2 shows significant losses in individual programmes, funds and policies covered by the EU budget.

For Cohesion Funding, the total losses accumulated throughout the current MFF 2021-2017 are estimated at EUR 47.4 billion, which accounts for 12.2 % of total funding. For the common agricultural policy, based on inflation during the period 2020-2023 and expected inflation for the period 2024-2027, total real losses are estimated at EUR 30.3 billion, which accounts for 8.5 % of total funding.

The pure loss of purchasing power of available Recovery and Resilience Facility funds between 2021 and 2025 is estimated at EUR 20.9 billion, which accounts for 7.6% of total expenditure. In view of the above: 1.
Has the Commission calculated the purchasing power losses of the current MFF due to inflation levels?
Does it intend, in the context of its proposal for the next MFF, to put forward measures to address the effects of inflation and protect the real value of EU budget funds?
How does it view the proposed creation of a dedicated mechanism that exceeds MFF ceilings to protect EU programme funds from inflationary pressures?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.3.2025) The ceilings of the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) for 2021-2027 are expressed in 2018 prices and the adjustment to current prices is done based on a fixed annual deflator of 2% (article 4(2) of the MFF Regulation1).
This long-standing adjustment mechanism, in use since 2007, has the advantage of providing predictability for the EU programme resources over the duration of the MFF.

The Commission has assessed the impact of the high inflation on the real value of MFF expenditure in the context of the Mid-term revision of the MFF proposed in June 20232 based on the forecast at that time, as discussed in the Staff Working Document accompanying the MFF revision (SWD(2023) 336 final3). The impact of inflation is being assessed together with all the other features of the MFF.

The current MFF has instruments over and above the MFF expenditure ceilings that provide flexibility to address unexpected needs, including inflationary pressures. These instruments were reinforced in the MFF revision, with an increase in the flexibility instrument and the Solidarity and Emergency Aid Reserve and the introduction of the EU recovery instrument.
The design of any future flexibility tool remains to be decided in the context of the next MFF.
